title: Introducing New Times Corps Members

body_markdown:
Twenty-one students are joining The New York Times Corps, the newsroom’s talent-mentorship program for undergraduates. Read more below from the Early Career Programs team.


[The New York Times Corps](https://www.nytco.com/careers/newsroom/times-corps/) , the newsroom’s talent-mentorship program for aspiring journalists, is welcoming a new cohort of 21 college students from across the country. The participants will spend multiple years learning from Times journalists.


Each student is matched with a newsroom mentor, from whom they receive regular career guidance and feedback. Virtual training sessions complete the experience, which ends upon college graduation. Students who finish the program may have the opportunity to visit New York and The Times in person.

The Times Corps is designed for undergraduates who are pursuing journalism and who demonstrate that they would particularly benefit from advice from working journalists. Nearly 100 students have joined the program since it began in 2022.


Times Corps alumni work at local and national news organizations across the country. A number of participants have earned placements in other prestigious journalism programs and training opportunities.


We plan to open applications for the next class in spring 2027. You can[learn more about the Times Corps and other early career opportunities at The Times here.](https://www.nytco.com/careers/entry-level/)


— Ted Kim and Carla Correa
